suggestions.title: Close reconcile closes a building/failed task whose delivered PR was merged, so merged work ends as closed rather than done
suggestions.evidence: CLOSE_RECONCILE_SKIPPED = ['done','closed','review'] (line 92), so building and failed tasks are reconciled. builds.ts:1693-1710 at the head keeps a task whose build delivered a GitHub PR in 'building' until ci-loop.ts:311 moves it to review on green checks. After 3 red rounds, ci-loop moves it to failed with the PR still open. closerVerdict only checks that the newest closed event's actor has triage or above. It cannot tell a merge-driven close from a manual one. The PR body says 'A task in review is left to the PR reconcile of #1414, so a merge that closes the issue still ends in done'. That holds only for review.
suggestions.failurePath:
Setup: PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE=1, and an imported issue task in a GitHub project.
1. The build step delivers PR #M. The task stays in building while CI is pending or red (ci-fix rounds).
2. A maintainer merges PR #M on GitHub, and its body or squash message carries 'closes #N'. GitHub closes issue #N, and the closed event's actor is the merger, who has write access.
3. On the next intake sweep (within 5 minutes), seenOpen holds the key and the state reads closed. closerVerdict returns trusted, and the phase is still building.
4. transitionTodos(..., 'closed') at line 569 sets phase closed and stops the active ci-fix steps. The ci-loop then sees phase != building and never advances the task.

Result: work that was merged is recorded as closed (canceled), not review or done. The same happens to a failed task whose PR is merged anyway. Not blocking: it needs a closing reference and a merge during the CI window, and ticket #1406 does ask for close-on-issue-close.

Possible fixes: skip tasks whose latest build has a prNumber, or treat a closed event that carries commit_id or comes from a PR as not this reconcile's to act on.

suggestions.title: An orchestrate failure after import leaves the task unorchestrated for good and holding a cap slot
suggestions.evidence: take() counts the import, adds seenOpen, then calls orchestrateTodo in a try/catch that only increments errors (lines 405-411) and returns 'imported'. On later sweeps the issue's ref is in claimedRefs (lines 469-471), so it is skipped as claimed, and nothing re-orchestrates a todo-phase github-issue task. projectFull counts it as in flight (NOT_IN_FLIGHT excludes only done and closed).
suggestions.failurePath: orchestrateTodo throws after importGithubIssue succeeds, for example because the chief's agent loses its model between chiefCanOrchestrate and the call, or the DB is busy. The task stays in phase todo with no chief thread. Every later sweep counts it as claimed and never retries orchestration. It also keeps one of the project's 3 slots until a person starts or closes it, and three such failures stop intake for the project. The Risk section calls this 'the window is one sweep', but the effect lasts until someone acts. A retry for poller-imported todo tasks that have no thread would close the gap.

suggestions.title: Spec 28 §4 P5a still says every closed issue closes its task, and does not mention the opt-in switch
suggestions.failurePath: docs/pr-review.md step 5 asks for docs/spec to change when behavior changes. Spec 28 §4 P5a (lines 139 and 142) still says the poller runs and that 被领的 issue 在 GitHub 上关了 → 对账收尾为 closed. At this head the poller is off unless PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE is set (config.ts envFlag, scheduler.ts issueIntakeRunOf). Its reconcile closes a task only on an open-to-closed change this process saw, by a closer with triage or above (issue-intake.ts:549-558). A task is left open when its outside author closed the issue, when the issue closed while the server was down, or when the task is in review. Someone who reads spec 28 as the P5 design, for example segment 2/3 or the P8 rollout, would expect every claimed issue that closes to close its task, and to be polled without opt-in. Only the README and the §8 ledger row record the narrower rule and the switch.

With the regression, closerVerdict picks the maintainer's old closed event, returns 'trusted', and transitionTodos closes the task and stops its active steps on an outsider's action. Round 2's B2 fix was meant to rule this out. Suggested test: two closed events, older by OWNER and newer by an outsider, then assert closeSkipped=1 and that the phase is unchanged.

With the regression, newestLabeler returns 'label-removed' and the issue is never taken, sweep after sweep. Suggested tests: (a) an unrelated unlabeled event after the labeled event, then assert the issue is taken; (b) a labeled and an unlabeled event with the same created_at, unlabeled with the higher id, then assert it is not taken.

suggestions.title: Issue body is imported as it reads at sweep time, not as it read when the maintainer labeled it, and the chief sees it as the user's own request
suggestions.failurePath: 1. An outside author opens a harmless issue. 2. A user with triage applies ready-for-agent, so D5 passes (labelerVerdict, issue-intake.ts:339-355). 3. Before the next 5-minute sweep, the author edits the body, which the author can always do. 4. take() calls importGithubIssue (issue-intake.ts:384). That reads the current body into todo.spec (github-issues.ts:163). orchestrateTodo then runs on its own. 5. buildOrchestratePrompt (packages/shared/src/records/prompts.ts:288-307) quotes the body as '任务原文' in the chief's user message. Nothing marks it as written by a GitHub issue author, possibly from outside the repo. The chief's conventions let it save_memory when 'the user explicitly asks', and saved memories are rendered into composeChiefSystemPrompt's 记忆 section (chief.ts:748+). So the edited text can reach the chief's tools, and through the model, the system layer on later turns. No code path puts the body into the system layer directly, so D5 holds as written. The PR's Risk section names the edit-after-label case. Options: refuse an issue whose updated_at is later than the newest ready-for-agent labeled event, or add a provenance line in the orchestrate prompt for github-issue tasks.

suggestions.title: Labels applied through an app (and so by agent sessions) count as the human labeler, and the projection drops performed_via_github_app
suggestions.failurePath: The PR's own capture (docs/verify/1406/fixtures/events-1406.json) shows #1406's ready-for-agent was applied with actor xiechimon and performed_via_github_app.slug 'claude'. githubIssueEvents keeps only actor.login (github.ts:593). Agent sessions here label issues routinely (the issue-label gate wants a state label on every open issue). An imported issue body that steers its agent into labeling another issue ready-for-agent through the owner's app or gh login therefore makes that issue pass D5 on a later sweep. This does not break D5 as written, and the PR's Risk section names it. This was a suggestion in run 1 and is still open: keep performed_via_github_app in GithubIssueEvent and in the 'candidate taken' log or the task record, so labels applied by an agent can be audited or treated separately later.

suggestions.title: The close reconcile covers every github-issue task, not only issues the poller took
suggestions.failurePath: toReconcile (issue-intake.ts:663-673) takes every todo with sourceKind 'github-issue' outside done, closed and review. That includes tasks a person imported by hand from an open issue and tasks the webhook imported. reconcileClosed marks any of them seenOpen when it reads the issue as open (line 544). When a user with triage then closes the issue, transitionTodos(..., 'closed') runs and stopActiveStepsAfterExit stops the task's active steps, even if a person is building it right now. The ticket's failure mode limits this to issues the poller took ('被领的 issue 在 GitHub 上关了'). The README documents the wider behaviour and the closer must have triage, so it can be undone (reopen) and it is not a security hole. It is still a scope widening the user should agree to.
